inputs.tags: A lush neo-soul track anchored by a warm Rhodes electric piano playing rich ninth and thirteenth chords over a loose, soulful live drum groove with heavy use of ghost notes and rim shots. A fretless bass provides a melodic, singing counterline beneath the harmony. The lead vocalist is a powerful, expressive woman who moves fluidly between a smoky chest voice and an airy falsetto, employing tasteful melismatic runs and bluesy bends. A tight three-part vocal harmony stack fills out the chorus. A muted trumpet and alto saxophone trade fills during the instrumental bridge, channeling the spirit of classic 1970s soul. The production is warm and analog-sounding, with subtle tape saturation and a slight room ambience.
inputs.lyrics:
[Intro — Rhodes piano and brushed drums]
[Verse 1]
You never call when the neon goes dark
Just send a signal like an afterthought
I learned to read the silence between the lines
And honey that's a language I know too well by now
[Pre-Chorus]
Maybe I'm the fool who kept the door wide open
Maybe you're the draft that keeps on blowing through
[Chorus]
I'm done rewriting your story in my head
Done saving room for someone who's already gone
I'll keep the record on
But I'll stop singing your part
[Instrumental Bridge — Muted trumpet and alto saxophone trade phrases]
[Verse 2]
The coffee shop still plays our favourite song
I ordered something different, stayed too long
But every note just proved that I was right
To let the whole thing go before it burned my life
[Final Chorus — Layered harmonies, fuller arrangement]
[Outro — Rhodes vamp fades, final bass note sustains]
